reasoning: The transition engine is being implemented right now, and this message forbids an output that implementation may currently be producing. That is the definition the skill gives a correction: it 'changes the goal or the constraints of work in flight', and the Director's response is to 'change that work's goal and replan what is left', never to 'open a new task alongside the old one'. The skill also warns that the same words go either way depending on situation — 'the same sentence, word for word, is an idea when nothing related is being built and a correction when something related is' — and here something related is being built, so it is a correction, not an idea or a fresh instruction. The prohibition is the repair stated aloud ('take that part out'), and the skill says such a clause 'names what the replan will contain, so it is the correction's own goal in other words; naming it as an instruction of its own re-opens as fresh work the very thing the correction just changed' — so no second act and no second row. It is not a halt: the engine keeps running toward the same goal with a narrower constraint, and 'a halt is for the work itself stopping — nothing left to pursue'. It is not a decision either: it carries no standing-rule marker ('from this point on', 'always', 'note this for yourself') and it does not settle an open choice inside work that proceeds as planned — it changes what the running work must produce, so 'the remainder has to be replanned'. Volume and emphasis do not add an act; 'tone does not decide this'. On the numbers, the skill is explicit that 'replanning takes on nothing that did not already exist: the board gains no row, and the count of new pieces of work the turn produces is zero' — hence creates_work false, work_items 0, attaches_to_existing_work true, and the ticket operation is the replan of the piece already in hand (T3). Dimensions are named because the one exception to naming none is 'a correction, which changes work already running: saying what that work now touches is the whole point of it' — the ban changes what the engine may produce (product value and behaviour) and what the viewer sees between pictures (the user's path and the design). Specialists are the smallest set that corrected work may need: the developer, since the engine itself must change, and the spec author, since 'behaviour changes beyond what the spec already says' once a whole class of output is ruled out.
